newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens readies to evacuate Greeks from Albania.
newsitem.headline: Athens readies to evacuate Greeks from Albania.

text.p: Greece was working on a plan to evacuate its citizens from its troubled Balkan neighbour Albania as soon necessary, Defence Ministry officials said on Thursday.
A Greek navy frigate was on its way to the Greek island of Corfu, across from the southern Albanian port of Sarande, to be ready to ferry people to Greek soil, they said.
"There is a meeting at the Defence Ministry examining safe ways to evacuate Greek citizens from Albania," a senior ministry official told Reuters. "The operation will take place only if necessary."
He said the option of sending an air force cargo plane to Tirana was being examined at the meeting but there was concern that it might not be able to land at the capital's airport.

There are about 30 Greek diplomats in Tirana and an army of Greek reporters both in the capital and southern Albania, now mostly controlled by insurgents armed with weapons looted from military depots.

Greece, gravely concerned with the crisis at its northern border, sent a navy minesweeper with humanitarian aid to Sarande on Thursday. It is also sending its Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos to Tirana on Friday to help defuse the crisis.

The United States has began a military evacuation from Albania of non-essential U.S. embassy employees and other Americans who wish to leave, while Italy also said it was evacuating about 400 foreign nationals.
